title: Police Called It An Accident. A Bullet Said Otherwise. Who Was The Man On The Green Bicycle?
description:
On July 5th, 1919, 21-year-old Bella Wright was found dead on a lonely Leicestershire lane. Police initially ruled it a bicycle accident — until a post-mortem revealed a bullet had passed clean through her skull, fired from close range.

Witnesses recalled a man on a distinctive green bicycle riding beside Bella that evening. Seven months later, dredgers pulled that very bicycle from Leicester's River Soar, deliberately weighted down. The frame number led police to Ronald Light, an engineer who admitted riding with Bella but denied killing her.

At trial, defended by the legendary Marshall Hall, the jury deliberated just twenty minutes before returning a not guilty verdict. The revolver was never found. No motive was ever established. Light lived another 55 years and never explained why he really ran.
